chapters.title: When two documents seem to disagree
chapters.lede: Overviews and Quick References explain and route. Detailed policies, handbooks and approved tools govern the rule.

blocks.title: The authority order
rows: Current external **law or provider rule** (e.g. Cambridge)
The Eduversal **canonical policy / handbook** named in the Register
The approved **operational instrument** that implements it
**Quick References**, presentations and summaries — including these guides
check: Current external law or provider rule, where applicable
Quick Reference documents, presentations, and communication summaries

blocks.title: Every rule carries one of four labels
rows: Required by Indonesian law or a binding ministry rule
An approved Eduversal standard — never presented as an external requirement
Supports quality but is not mandatory on its own
check: [Eduversal network policy] - an approved Eduversal standard adopted for partner schools
[Recommended practice]

blocks.title: A summary never changes the rule
blocks.text: Overviews, Quick References, training and communication documents must keep the **same authority status** as their source — they must not upgrade a recommendation into a requirement. That is why every page of these guides links back to its live document.
check: must preserve the same authority status and must not upgrade a recommendation

chapters.title: Collect evidence once
chapters.lede: Use it at the correct level. Keep developmental and evaluative spaces separate. Add a new task only when it adds new information or meets a clear governing requirement.

blocks.title: The no-duplication check
blocks.lead: Before asking for a new form, upload, meeting, observation, tracker or data entry:
points: Does this information **already exist** in an approved system or document?
Can the existing evidence be **linked or aggregated** instead?
Is it **required by policy**, or has it grown informally over time?
Does it create a **new score** that another system already owns?
check: Does this information already exist in an approved system or document?
Collect evidence once. Use it at the correct level.

blocks.title: When capacity is not enough
blocks.intro: Never skip a mandatory requirement silently — and never create paperwork just to look compliant.

steps.title: Escalate early
steps.text: The Principal or Academic Coordinator tells the Eduversal module owner.

steps.title: One of three answers
steps.text: An approved adjustment that keeps the standard, extra support, or a documented timeline.

check: A school should not silently skip a mandatory requirement
an approved implementation adjustment that preserves the standard, additional support, or a documented timeline

blocks.title: Everyday discipline
do: Submit the **strongest existing** evidence for School Appraisal; link one source to several expectations.
Use **existing meetings** and **one** action tracker (owner, action, due date, status).
Treat Latihan.id, Edunav or the designated system as the **system of record**.
Give each supported teacher **one growth priority** (two at most) per semester.
dont: Create a document only for the visit when the practice does not exist yet — record the gap honestly.
Make teachers re-type data an approved system already holds.
Copy induction journals, mentor notes or coaching content into appraisal records.
Turn indicators into a parallel KPI system.
check: Schools should submit the strongest existing evidence, not manufacture new documents for the visit
One agreed action tracker should capture owner, action, due date, and status
with a maximum of two per semester
